QF.id: XIII Introduction to the Underlying Markets_80

question.text: Which underlying market requires the most direct tracking of foreign economic conditions and central bank actions?

answer.text: The currency market — because currency prices are influenced by multiple local and global factors, including interest-rate conditions and central bank actions
The equity market — because foreign central bank actions determine stock prices in India
The bond market — because Indian bond yields are entirely set by foreign central banks
All three markets are equally and directly influenced by foreign central bank actions

explanation.text: The Logic: Currency prices are influenced by a combination of local and global factors, including interest-rate conditions and central bank actions. Tracking foreign economic conditions and central bank actions is therefore most directly relevant to the currency market. The Trap: Saying that foreign central banks directly determine Indian stock prices or that they entirely set Indian bond yields overstates the influence; equity and bond markets are also driven by domestic factors and are not directly determined by foreign central banks. Note: The currency-market description is one of influence by multiple factors, not absolute determination by monetary-policy differentials alone.
